Pk Parameter: i=1 |Fi | Question: Is there a graph G such that hom(Fi , G) = mi for every i ∈ [k]? It is open if this problem is fixed-parameter tractable, or at least the complexity class XP, that is, solvable in polynomial time for each fixed parameter value. We prove that the problem is in XP if the Fi are stars.

statement: ▶ Remark 16. We remark that for constraint graphs from a class of bounded treewidth, the problem UnHomRec is in NP since counting homomorphisms is in polynomial time. It remains open, whether there are classes for which this problem is NP-complete.
context: Proof. We can assume that the graph G has at most i=1 hi |V (Fi )| vertices by the observation from [4]. An NPNP machine first non-deterministically guesses G and hi different homomorphisms h : Fi → G. We verify that there are no other homomorphisms by calling the NP oracle. ◀ ▶ Remark 16. We remark that for constraint graphs from a class of bounded treewidth, the problem UnHomRec is in NP since counting homomorphisms is in polynomial time. It remains open, whether there are classes for which this problem is NP-complete. The 2-Round-3-Colouring problem is complete for Σp2 (see Thm. 11.4 in [1]). Its containment in Σp2 is obvious, since it is of the form “x ∈ L if and only if y exists such that f (x, y) ∈ Non-3-Colouring” and we recall that Non-3-Colouring ∈ coNP. 2-Round-3-Colouring Input: Graph F .
